intro: Travellers once arrived at this gate after long days on the road. You are at Karatay Han, a caravanserai in Kayseri province, built in 1240 for the emir Celâleddin Karatay. Look at its portal: human-headed figures and animal reliefs in the richest sequence of Seljuk carving.
history: The han was built in 1240 for the emir Celâleddin Karatay, and it was the grandest stop on the Kayseri–Malatya road. The human-headed figures, the lions and the geometric carving of its portal make one of the richest sequences of Seljuk ornament. Together with a mosque, a bath and a tomb, it forms a small complex.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the portal and the covered hall, then the bath and the tomb of Karatay.
facts: Did you know? Karatay's endowment deed requires that travellers be received at the han without regard to religion or sect. And the human-headed figures and lions of its portal make one of the richest sequences of Seljuk ornament.
outro: This brings our tour of Karatay Han to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Safe travels, and enjoy your visit.
